title: Probe case
description: Declarative probe against the pinned vercel/serve reference. Each probe either spawns a serve instance against a fixture and runs an ordered list of HTTP requests (the default) OR runs a process-level CLI invocation to capture exit code + stdout + stderr.

id.description: Probe id. Optional; defaults to the file name without extension.

description.description: Free-form prose displayed in the result report.

files.description: Map of fixture-relative path to file content. Strings are written as utf-8; objects with a base64 field are written as binary.

serveJson.description: Optional serve.json contents. Written verbatim into <fixture>/serve.json before the server starts.

serveArgs.description: Extra command-line arguments passed to `node third_party/serve/build/main.js` after the runner's own --listen / --no-clipboard / --no-port-switching.

runner.description: Runner-level options governing how the case is spawned and how its results are filtered against `target=irserve`. Added in change 002 (Stage 5b).

skipAutoListen.description: When true the runner does NOT inject `--listen <port>` into the spawned process. Used by SRV-CLI-001 default-port probes. Requires `defaultPortScenario`.

defaultPortScenario.description: Required when `skipAutoListen` is true. `no-flag-no-env`: runner reserves port 3000 (aborts if occupied) and HTTP-probes 3000. `env-var`: runner allocates a free port P, exports `PORT=P` into the spawned process env, and HTTP-probes P.

l0.description: Per-anchor partition applied when running against `target=irserve`. Cases without an `l0` block are skipped under `target=irserve`.

clean.description: Anchor names that must match the reference snapshot (subject to volatile-header masking and the may-differ overlays below). Anchors not in `clean` and not in `divergent` are stripped from the diff (treated as informational).

divergent.description: Anchor names recorded as informational only. Their request still executes against irserve, but the result is removed from BOTH sides of the diff.

bodyMayDiffer.description: Anchor names whose response body is may-differ (e.g. HTML 404 body per D-003). Strips body.length / body.sha256 / body.preview AND `content-length` for those anchors.

contentLengthMayDiffer.description: Anchor names whose `content-length` header is may-differ but whose body bytes are must-match (e.g. JSON 404 envelope where serve uses chunked transfer-encoding).

exitCodeMayDiffer.description: CLI-mode anchor names where exit code is may-differ but must be non-zero (per ORC-062 must-match: `exit=non-zero`). The runner asserts both sides are non-zero then strips `exitCode`.

snapshot.description: Optional snapshot configuration. Used by `tools/probe/run.mjs --snapshot=update|verify` to control how the canonical snapshot is built and compared. See tools/probe/snapshots/_schema.json.

volatileHeaders.description: Lowercase header names whose values vary between runs against the same fixture (e.g., `last-modified` when the fixture is materialized fresh each run). The snapshot records the observed value but `verify` treats the value as a wildcard. Defaults to ["last-modified"] when this field is absent.

volatileBodies.description: Names of requests whose response body is volatile across runs even after the runner's path normalization (the runner replaces the absolute fixture directory with `<FIXTURE_ROOT>` before computing body sha256 / preview, so listings are usually stable; this list is the escape hatch for cases where some other source of nondeterminism remains). For those requests the snapshot still records body length / sha256 / preview, but `verify` masks those fields. The body's `kind` is still asserted. Defaults to [].

extraTrackedHeaders.description: Lowercase response-header names to add to the runner's tracked-header allowlist for this case only. The runner records and asserts these headers in the snapshot. Use when a probe sets a custom header (e.g. `X-Custom`) that is not in the global allowlist.

cli.description: Process-level CLI invocations to capture (alternative to `requests` for non-HTTP probes such as `--help`, `--version`, two-positional-arg failure). The runner spawns `node third_party/serve/build/main.js <args>` per entry, captures exit code + stdout + stderr, and produces a CLI snapshot under tools/probe/snapshots/<id>.json. A case must define EITHER `requests` OR `cli`, not both.

args.description: Arguments passed verbatim after the serve entry path.

name.description: Stable identifier of this request within the probe (used as a section heading in the report).

path.description: Request path. Must include the leading slash. Use percent-encoded characters as-is.

redirect.description: How fetch handles redirects. Default 'manual' (so the runner records the 301/302 itself rather than chasing it). Ignored when mode is 'raw'.

mode.description: Request transport. 'fetch' (default) uses Node's fetch and may normalize the URL path (collapsing '..', decoding '%2e%2e', collapsing '//'). 'raw' opens a net.Socket and sends the literal request line bytes; use it for wire-level probes such as path-traversal verification. The runner injects Host and Connection: close in raw mode unless the case provides them.
